# edgecenter_websec_source_group (Resource)

WebSec source group: the origins that protected resources and their locations forward requests to.

Every attribute is updated in place; nothing forces a replacement.

A group that resources or locations still use is not deleted: the API would delete them together with the group, so the provider stops and lists them. To point a resource at another group and delete the old group in the same apply, keep `create_before_destroy` in the `lifecycle` of the old group from the start: Terraform takes the flag from state, and with it the resource is updated before the old group is deleted. Without the flag, move the resources to the new group in one apply and remove the old group in the next one. If a group is itself replaced with `create_before_destroy`, the new one needs another name because names are unique within the client.

Import with `<group_id>` or `resource:<resource_id>`. The group id is the number in `source_group` of a resource, and `resource:<resource_id>` imports the group that `edgecenter_websec_resource` uses. A resource moved from the old protection API keeps the id of its `edgecenter_protection_resource`, so the second form needs only the id from the old state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "edgecenter" {
  permanent_api_token = "251$d3361.............1b35f26d8"
}

resource "edgecenter_websec_source_group" "example_com" {
  name        = "example.com origins"
  description = "Origins of example.com"

  source {
    source = "203.0.113.10"
    weight = 60
  }

  source {
    source       = "backup.example.com:8080"
    mode         = "backup"
    weight       = 40
    max_fails    = 3
    fail_timeout = 10
    comment      = "Second data center"
  }

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the group, up to 255 characters, unique within the client.
- `source` (Block List, Min: 1) Sources of the group, kept in the order given. More than one source works only when the multiple sources feature is enabled for the client. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--source))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the group.
- `use_next` (Boolean) Pass a request on to the next source when the current one fails. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedblock--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source`

Required:

- `source` (String) Host name or IPv4 address of the origin with an optional port, for example `203.0.113.10` or `origin.example.com:8080`, without a scheme or a path. The API also checks that a host name resolves and that the origin is not in a private network.

Optional:

- `comment` (String) Comment on the source, up to 255 characters.
- `fail_timeout` (Number) Time in seconds in which `max_fails` failed attempts make the source unavailable, and for which it then stays unavailable, at least 1. Defaults to `1`.
- `max_fails` (Number) Number of failed attempts within `fail_timeout` after which the source is considered unavailable, at least 1. Defaults to `1`.
- `mode` (String) `primary`, `backup` (gets requests only when the primary sources fail) or `down` (gets no requests). Defaults to `primary`.
- `weight` (Number) Weight of the source in load balancing, from 1 to 100. The weights of all sources of the group add up to at most 100 whatever their mode, so a third source with the default weight does not fit. Defaults to `50`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import edgecenter_websec_source_group.example_com 7
terraform import edgecenter_websec_source_group.example_com resource:12345
```
